concerns.text: Spec US1-AC-002 requires 'Non-English and gibberish text is filtered out'. Tasks T014b and T014c implement these filters, but T014c ('gibberish filtering logic... entropy-based heuristic') lacks a specific tag or explicit reference to US1-AC-002 in its description, relying on the task title. While the description implies coverage, the lack of a direct `[US1-AC-002]` tag or explicit 'See US1-AC-002' reference makes traceability ambiguous compared to T014b which is tagged. This risks the implementer missing the specific acceptance criteria for gibberish filtering.

Spec US2-AC-005 requires 'filter_applied metadata contributes to the control proxy score'. Task T022 describes 'Implement logic to calculate filter_applied contribution... (e.g., A positive increment is applied if the flag is present.)'. However, T022 is not tagged with `[US2-AC-005]` or `[US2]` in the task list header (it has `[US2]` in the description but the header format `[ID] [P?] [Story] Description` is inconsistent here, showing `[ ] T022 [US2]` which is correct, but the description is vague on the *exact* logic required by the spec vs an example). More critically, T021 (extraction) is tagged `[US2]`, but T022 (calculation) is the one actually fulfilling AC-005. The task description uses 'e.g.' which suggests the logic is not fully defined, potentially leaving the specific contribution logic (required by AC-005) undefined in the task itself.

Spec US3-AC-008 requires 'Shapiro-Wilk test is performed on residuals'. Tasks T033a and T033b implement this. T033b is tagged `[US3]` and mentions the spec in the description. However, T033a (residual calculation) is not explicitly tagged with `[US3-AC-008]` or `[US3]` in the header (it shows `[ ] T033a [US3]` which is correct). The concern is that the *calculation* of residuals (T033a) is a prerequisite for the test (T033b) mandated by AC-008. While T033a is present, the lack of a direct tag linking it to the specific AC-008 requirement (which mandates the *test on residuals*, implying the calculation) makes the traceability of the 'residuals' part of the requirement slightly weaker than the test itself. A more robust tag would be `[US3-AC-008]` on T033a as well.

Task T004b is tagged `[US0]`. The spec does not define a 'US0'. User stories start at US1. This is a stale or incorrect tag. The task content ('Verify SC-004...') is valid, but the tag `[US0]` references a non-existent user story, creating confusion in the traceability matrix.

Tasks T014b and T014c are both tagged `[US1-AC-002]`. While this is good, the task list format `[ID] [P?] [Story] Description` usually expects a single story tag like `[US1]`. Having two tasks tagged with the same specific AC ID is acceptable for traceability, but the header format `[US1-AC-002]` is non-standard compared to other tasks which use `[US1]`. This inconsistency in tagging style (AC-level vs Story-level) might confuse automated parsers expecting `[US#]`.
